newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar's Emir speaks of country's gas potential.
newsitem.headline: Qatar's Emir speaks of country's gas potential.

text.p: Qatar's ruler Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al-Thani said on Monday the Gulf Arab state would become a leading exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in the next few years.

"The coming few years will establish the status of Qatar as a major exporter of liquefied gas to international markets proportional to the large reserves of natural gas which the country has in the North Field," the Emir Hamad bin Khalifa Al-Thani said in an opening address to a gas conference in Doha.
Qatar has the world's third largest gas reserves behind Russia and Iran and is planning three multi-billion, foreign backed LNG projects to capitalise on growing Asia power demand.
"Work has already begun to execute the second project for exporting Qatari liquefied gas," he told an audience of foreign and local oil and gas executives.
He also called for the construction of industrial projects in Qatar to use gas produced from its giant North Field, the largest non-associated gas field in the world.

"Qatar is keen on providing the suitable climate for the success of industrial projects that are based on intensive use of gas and on opening the way for shareholding in them for international companies," he said.
The "Second Doha conference on natural gas" runs from March 17 to March 19.
